The FOMC’s communication is broadly growth-positive—solid activity and strong labor markets—yet tempered by inflation still below 2%. This mix aligns with the expectations-augmented Phillips curve and New Keynesian evidence that inflation is driven by expected inflation and marginal costs rather than unemployment alone (Friedman–Phelps; Galí & Gertler; Woodford; Christiano, Eichenbaum & Evans). Low market-based inflation compensation suggests subdued expected inflation, consistent with theory that expectations anchor nominal rates and near-term price dynamics. The commitment to a symmetric 2% goal and gradual, accommodative policy fits interest-rate rule frameworks and evidence that abrupt tightening depresses future consumption and real activity (Sims & Zha; Canzoneri, Cumby & Diba), justifying a measured path. Net tone: moderately positive on growth and employment, cautious on inflation, and gradualist on policy.
